name: peel-flow
title: Peel Flow
description: A full-bleed closing-CTA band running a real powder-coat levelling simulation: a scrolling material band where short-wavelength orange peel vanishes in about a second and long-wavelength peel survives for minutes, per Orchard's lambda^4 levelling equation, with cure-shrinkage telegraphing keeping the already-frozen region alive behind the band.
instruction: Build <PeelFlow headline? headlineFit? headlineY? speed? paused? children? className?> as a full-bleed WebGL2 closing-CTA band running a REAL simulation, not an analytic per-pixel field like weld-pool: a fixed 192x108 float texture h(x,y) (RG32F via EXT_color_buffer_float, R=height G=cure-age; RGBA8 16-bit-packed fallback when the extension is absent) is advanced every frame by a ping-ponged fragment-shader sim pass, then a separate shading pass reads the current field and lights it. THE RING BUFFER: the field's 192x108 storage never resizes or resets on scroll -- each texel's fixed storage coordinate IS its physical identity, and only its INTERPRETED screen position shifts: screenX = fract(texelU.x + scrollFrac), where scrollFrac accumulates at BAND_SPEED_COEF=0.055*min(w,h)_css_px/s converted into a fraction-of-lap-per-second via (0.055*min(w,h))/hostWidthCss (the SIM_W term cancels out of the conversion, so lap speed depends only on host aspect ratio). Three zones, fixed screen-space fractions: 0.00-0.22 deposition (a bell reciprocates vertically on a 3.1s triangle wave over field-height fraction 0.12-0.88, laying a Gaussian fan gated by a Faraday starvation factor 1/(1+2.4*|grad h|), salted with hash-based noise seeded from (texel index, floor(scroll distance)) -- never Math.random() or performance.now(), so state is exactly reproducible from (dt-sequence, scrollFrac) alone); 0.22-0.78 melt/levelling (viscosity ramps 3000->100->3000 Pa.s across the zone on a smoothstepped parabola, and every frame applies h -= k(x)*dt*biharm(h) using the 13-point discrete biharmonic stencil [center 20, 4 orthogonal-adjacent -8, 4 diagonal-adjacent 2, 4 two-away-orthogonal 1, weights sum to zero so it is mean-preserving] -- substepped as two half-dt passes per frame, comfortably inside the stencil's CFL bound k*dt/dx^4<=1/32; k is calibrated as K_BASE=0.0213 texel^4/s at eta=100 (melt centre) so that tau(0.2mm)~1.0s, tau(0.5mm)~39s, tau(1.0mm)~10min reproduce the spec's own table via the stencil's (2*pi/lambda)^4 eigenvalue -- deliberately calibrated against that table rather than the raw SI Orchard constants, which are ~33x faster and would trip the kill criterion of levelling everything instantly; k is additionally scaled by kAspectScale = (min(w,h)/W)/0.278 so total melt dose stays roughly aspect-invariant); 0.78-1.00 frozen (k=0, BUT a second, unforced process keeps this zone alive: cure-shrinkage telegraphing accumulates cure-age per texel and grows h += (h - local4NeighborMean)*(1-exp(-age/7.5))*0.10*dt, amplifying whatever long-wavelength relief survived levelling as the film ages toward full cure -- this is what makes the already-passed region change between t=0 and t=5s by more than translation, per DECISIONS.md D3, verified on a CPU port of the sim step alone: cropping the frozen region and registering by the known scroll translation over 5s gives a residual-to-RMS fraction of 0.55 on h and 2.56 on |lap h|, far from the near-zero a translating still image would show). PRE-ROLL: a blank field takes a full scroll lap (tens of seconds at real speed) to populate the frozen zone, which would show an empty right third for the first minute of every mount -- so every entry path (mount, resize, reduced-motion, mode change) first fast-forwards deterministically through PRE_ROLL_FRACTION=0.95 of a lap using a coarse but CFL-safe dt (0.15s, a handful of fixed steps) BEFORE the first frame is ever drawn, so all three zones are populated immediately. SHADING (separate pass, samples the field directly, no analytic normal field): central-difference normal from four neighbor taps of h, reflected into a FIXED three-strip-light achromatic studio at elevations 62/34/11 degrees and azimuths 20/155/265 degrees -- the rig never moves, only the surface does, which is the deliberate inversion of grazing-light's static-relief-under-a-moving-light. Roughness comes from |lap(h)| (residual short-wavelength curvature), so the deposition third reads matte and the levelled/frozen thirds read glossy with zero hue change. HEADLINE: a knockout mask rasterized to a 2D-canvas texture (like weld-pool's glyph texture, box-blurred once per resize), sampled in FIXED screen space (not attached to the scrolling field) -- its specular lobe is suppressed by 0.7 and its colour is force-blended 22% toward the matte-deposit token stop, guaranteeing legibility independent of whatever the field is doing underneath at a given instant. TOKENS: five luminance stops from --background, --foreground, --ns-muted, --border read via getComputedStyle + a documentElement class MutationObserver, with a hard 0.18L floor enforced between adjacent stops (widens automatically rather than ever adding hue). --ns-accent DOES NOT EXIST AS A SHADER UNIFORM -- there is no u_accent anywhere in either fragment shader, so the project's most repeated defect (accent in a highlight/climactic moment) is structurally impossible rather than merely avoided; the CTA button rendered as DOM chrome above the canvas is the one legitimate place it appears, in its own fill/focus-ring classes. HOST: DPR capped at 1.5 with the same three-step adaptive-scale ladder as weld-pool (frame-time EMA, 900ms-sustained step-down, much-longer clean-stretch step-up, doubling wait per failure, never frame-counted); ResizeObserver on the host element (re-seeds the field, since kAspectScale changed); IntersectionObserver threshold 0 and visibilitychange both pause the rAF and re-read tokens on resume before the next draw. prefers-reduced-motion (and paused) run the same pre-roll, then a further fixed 444 steps at dt=1/60 to STATIC_TIME=7.4s past the pre-roll baseline (not from sim-time zero) -- chosen because the bell sits off both stroke ends there and all three zones already carry seeded material -- and draw exactly one frame; the seed is fully deterministic so that frame is byte-stable indefinitely.
useWhen: Pick peel-flow for a closing CTA band whose surface is a coating actually levelling under heat -- a scrolling material sim where short-wavelength texture visibly disappears while long-wavelength texture survives, in the same patch, at the same time. Pick convert-foil-block instead when the mechanic should be a transfer threshold (does the mark take at all, at 96C/0.34MPa) rather than a continuous levelling process; pick weld-pool instead for a hero (not a closing band) where the headline itself should be a liquid-metal height field lit and dented by the same analytic flow, with no scrolling material and no simulation state.
